### 1. Headline (tune sentences)

| | Baseline (never corrects) | v1 (first prompt) | v6 (best version) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mistakes caught | 0/7 | 6/7 | **7/7** |

The baseline gets the 3 correct sentences "right" by never doing anything, but it helps a learner with none of the 7 mistakes. v6 fixes 6 of them correctly.

**Catching vs fixing.** The last column counts mistakes the model noticed but fixed wrongly. On the tune sentences it stays small (1 to 2), so the real swings came from missed mistakes and from over-correcting. On unseen sentences the gap was much bigger (section 5).

Note: because every run is re-scored with the current answer key, v1 shows 5/7 matching here, not the 4/7 recorded at the time. We later accepted 你们有茶吗？ as a second right answer, which v1 had given.

### 4. Explanation language (flagged sentences)

We ask for explanations in English, because an A2 learner can't read a Chinese grammar explanation. Language is detected automatically (4+ Chinese characters in a row = Chinese), so treat it as approximate.

| Version | Flagged | English | Chinese |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1 | 8 | 0 (0%) | 8 |
| v2 | 8 | 0 (0%) | 8 |
| v3 | 5 | 0 (0%) | 4 |
| v4 | 9 | 4 (44%) | 5 |
| v5 | 5 | 3 (60%) | 2 |
| v6 | 8 | 4 (50%) | 4 |

English explanations only appeared once the prompt included worked examples written in English (v4). This is still our weakest area.

### 5. Early test-split run (v1, 32 unseen sentences)

This was run once by accident with v1 (see "Test-split runs"). It was not used to choose any change, but it shows how v1 behaved on sentences it had never seen.

| | Baseline | v1 |
|---|---|---|
| Mistakes caught | 0/21 | 19/21 (90%) |
| Corrections matching our answer | 0/21 | 3/21 (14%) |
| Correct sentences wrongly "fixed" | 0/11 | 6/11 (55%) |

| Mistake type | Sentences | Caught | Fixed right |
|---|---|---|---|
| word_order | 6 | 5 | 2 |
| extra_word | 4 | 4 | 1 |
| measure_word | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| question_structure | 3 | 2 | 0 |
| missing_particle | 2 | 2 | 0 |
| negation | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| other | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| unnatural | 1 | 1 | 0 |

v1 noticed almost every mistake but fixed very few correctly, the same "catching vs fixing" gap as on the tune sentences, only bigger. This is why later versions focused on the quality of the fix and on not over-correcting. The final test run will show how much of the tune-split improvement carries over to unseen sentences.

### 6. Reliability checks

- **Repeatable:** v1 was run twice on the tune sentences. The two runs were identical on every sentence (temperature 0), so differences between versions come from our changes, not chance.
- **Conversation:** across 6 versions, the waiter stayed in character in 30/30, 30/30, 30/30, 30/30, 30/30, 30/30 turns and remembered the order in 6/6, 6/6, 6/6, 6/6, 6/6, 6/6 chats (perfect every time). The waiter prompt never changed; only the mistake checker did.
- **Valid output:** every run produced a readable answer for every sentence (100%, 100%, 100%, 100%, 100%, 100%).

### 7. Caveats

- The tune split is only 10 sentences, so one sentence moves a score by 14 to 33 points. The final test on 32 unseen sentences is the real measure.
- "Matching our answer" is strict: a correct fix worded differently counts as wrong. A person should also check the corrections by hand.
- We picked v6 as best because it has the most matching fixes minus wrong "fixes" on the tune split.
